_comment: First half of the skill-interrupt pair (docs/05-architecture-domain-control-loops.md, docs/components/turn-pipeline.md 'Skills' interrupt-table row: 'Skill workflow (child)' gets the same cooperative-cancel treatment as a subagent). MUST be run with AUTO_APPROVE=0 -- otherwise run_scenario.sh's always-on auto-approve poller would resolve draft_note's own internal permission gate before the followup interrupt has a chance to land (the same reason that flag exists for testing a real denial). turn:1 calls draft_note directly (no discover_skills first, same shortcut interrupt-initial.json takes with shell_exec); its approval-gated UserInputRequestWorkflow child is still awaiting a signal when this returns. Run skill-interrupt-followup against the same -session shortly after: turn.go must cascade-cancel the in-flight skill child (and, one level deeper, its own approval child), fold the follow-up in as a user message, and let the model act on it. See skill-interrupt-followup.expect.sh.
